reviewed_route_classes.blocking_reason: These benchmarks directly instantiate inter-S1 disturbance and attenuation at benchmark-defined boundaries. Nool and The Specification Gap supply two admitted immutable direct non-canonical observations. Twining qualifies as a direct family but lacks recoverable exact treatment revision. CooperBench qualifies as a direct family because its first-party team harness coordinates integration-conflicting workers and exposes controlled feature ablations, but its committed 50-pair report is generated from flash run logs that are not pinned in the reviewed repository, so no CooperBench observation row is admitted.
The published ablations exercise native coordination mechanisms but score broad task/collaboration outcomes rather than an explicit interaction-generated disturbance and its attenuation.
The compared organization is benchmark-authored and/or deliberately removes recurring inter-S1 interference, so matched cost/quality/runtime rows are not direct S2 capability evidence.

Canonical S2 mechanisms exist, but current public result surfaces do not exercise them as direct native disturbance-to-attenuation capability observations. C.A.D.I.S. and ARES were explicitly re-reviewed in post-closure delta issue #592; Shep and Axocoatl were reviewed after their canonical admissions in issue #626 and likewise expose mechanism/microbenchmark surfaces without a direct S2 result.
The adapter/benchmark design is structurally promising, but the public leaderboard does not yet contain the multi-orchestrator result rows needed for a matched canonical cell.

closure_claim: Current public evidence contains six direct S2 disturbance benchmark families, two immutable direct non-canonical observations, and two native quantitative S2 proxy projections. The current reviewed canonical cohort still contains no canonical native direct observation and no matched canonical-harness S2 primary cell.
reopen_when: a canonical S2 harness publishes an explicit native inter-S1 disturbance-to-attenuation result
a materially matched benchmark evaluates two or more canonical systems exercising their own native or adapter-preserved S2 paths under one disturbance definition
MAO-Bench or a comparable benchmark publishes recoverable multi-orchestrator results with immutable system/model/configuration provenance and direct S2 semantics
do_not_reopen_for: another benchmark-scaffolded direct S2 observation without canonical native or adapter-preserved linkage
another broad collaboration or task-success score without an explicit S2 disturbance
another topology or framework benchmark whose coordination organization is benchmark-authored
another communication or token-efficiency metric without disturbance-to-attenuation closure
non_claim: This closure is not a zero S2 capability score and does not downgrade canonical S2 ownership. Nool and The Specification Gap provide direct evidence only for their benchmark-defined organizations. Twining and CooperBench likewise contribute direct-family coverage without canonical attribution; Twining lacks recoverable exact treatment revision, while CooperBench's committed 50-pair report lacks pinned flash-run logs for observation admission. Public full-dataset CooperBench trajectories are a separate evidence surface and are not silently substituted. The S2 primary remains frozen until materially new canonical native or matched evidence appears.
